details: CONFIRMED by reading the transcript shape on disk and the check at route-guard.py:113 (startswith on the whole string).
Effect: one wasted refused request per session that loaded the skill by slash command, then a wrong note on every Agent call
for the rest of the session, which tells the model the skill is missing when it is loaded. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: python3 over a real transcript printed: '<command-message>sdd:archive</command-message>\n<command-name>/sdd:archive</command-name>\n<command-args>...'
failing_case: The owner types `/delegate:delegate` in a session. Claude Code stores that user message as the string
'<command-message>delegate:delegate</command-message>\n<command-name>/delegate:delegate</command-name>\n...'
(seen in a real transcript under ~/.claude/projects: '<command-message>sdd:archive</command-message>\n<command-name>/sdd:archive</command-name>...').
skill_evidence() only accepts a string that starts with "/delegate:delegate" or "<command-name>/delegate:delegate", so loaded stays False:
the session's first Agent call is denied with "load the delegate skill first", and every later Agent call gets
"Routing note: the delegate skill was not loaded in this session". Expected: allowed silently, as for a Skill tool call.
The test (tests/test_spec_steps.py:546) writes the content as the bare string "/delegate:delegate", a shape Claude Code does not write, so it passes.
fix_hint: Match `<command-name>/delegate:delegate</command-name>` anywhere in a user message string (re.search), keep the bare "/delegate:delegate" start;
change the test fixture at tests/test_spec_steps.py:546 to the real shape.
pass_cases: 1. transcript user message content '<command-message>delegate:delegate</command-message>\n<command-name>/delegate:delegate</command-name>\n<command-args></command-args>' then an Agent call from the main session -> decide() returns None (allowed, no note).
2. transcript with a Skill tool_use input {"skill": "delegate:delegate"} -> None (works today, keeps working).
3. transcript with only an ordinary user prompt "do it" -> deny with "load the delegate skill first" (works today).

4. transcript whose user prompt merely mentions "<command-name>/delegate:delegate" in the middle of prose after other text -> still counted as loaded or not, as the fix decides, but a prompt "/front:front" must not count as loaded.
reason: tests/test_spec_steps.py:589 real command-message shape passes; /front:front still denied; fails on a1ea8c2
findings.summary: a typed /delegate:delegate is not seen as the skill loaded: real transcripts start the message with <command-message>, so the first agent is refused and every later one carries a false note

details: PLAUSIBLE: a paid run is needed to show the pass without the table; by reading, the prompt alone names the plan step and the skill's description matches it.
Principle 5 asks meaning to be tested with paid checks in several languages and with phrases that must not trigger; a check that the prompt answers for itself
measures nothing. Size: 15 minutes (prompts and one grader; no paid run here).
evidence: cat evals/plugin/spec-step-on-ru/prompt.md -> "Сделай так, чтобы список товаров сортировался по названию. ... Plan only, no code: stop when the spec step has written the change."
cat evals/plugin/no-spec-step/prompt.md -> "... Start the work through the project's usual agents and stop once a worker has been started and has replied."
failing_case: spec-step-on-en, -ru, -typo are meant to measure that a plain request ("сделай сортировку по названию") meets openspec:plan through the project's rules alone
(design section 2: "no slash command is needed ... The paid case spec-step-on measures that"). Each prompt adds "Plan only, no code: stop when the spec step has
written the change." openspec:plan's own description ("Use ... when the user asks to research, plan, design, or propose a change") then matches the prompt itself,
so the case passes with the [specs] setting and the steps table removed from CLAUDE.local.md. "Plan only, no code" also forbids any worker, so
no-worker-before-plan (max 0 delegate:worker) holds whatever happens. The control no-spec-step says "stop once a worker has been started", so the pair differ
in what the prompt asks, not only in the setting. Expected: the same plain request in both fixtures, the setting the only difference.
fix_hint: Give both twins one ending, for example "Start the work the way this project's rules say and stop at the first agent's reply"; grade spec-on by plan loaded and the off twin by worker started.
pass_cases: 1. spec-step-on-en/-ru/-typo prompts carry the feature request and the no-one-to-ask line only: no "plan", "spec" or "spec step" words, no "no code".
2. no-spec-step(-ru,-typo) prompts carry the same request text as their spec-step-on twin; the fixtures differ only in [specs] method and the rendered CLAUDE.local.md.
3. spec-step-on graders: openspec:plan loaded (min 1), and a grader that fails when a delegate:worker starts before the Skill call (or the run is capped before the build, stated in the case).
4. spec-step-on-bugfix keeps: no openspec:plan, a delegate:worker started.
reason: twin prompts identical, graders reworded; test_F5 fails before, passes now
findings.summary: the plain-words spec-step-on eval prompts name the answer ('Plan only ... stop when the spec step has written the change'), so they pass with the rendered steps table removed; the 'no worker before plan' grader is vacuous
